source_name: Кредобанк — Мережа відділень, банкоматів і терміналів самообслуговування
why_relevant: Bank branch/ATM locator pages are a machine-readable census of the estate — often the only per-bank ATM/self-service terminal count available at any point in time, and they date-stamp implicitly through change over time.

source_name: Банк Південний — Новини та мапа відділень/банкоматів
why_relevant: Mid-tier domestic-capital bank; news plus a device map and acquiring product pages that reveal terminal offerings and network scale.

source_name: А-Банк — еквайринг / бізнес-сторінки
why_relevant: Fast-growing card-centric private bank; acquiring and product pages disclose terminal types (incl. softPOS/virtual terminal) and occasionally network scale claims.

source_name: Sense Bank — corporate site / reporting
why_relevant: Nationalised former Alfa-Bank Ukraine, systemically important, with a large ATM estate (~700 devices reported); its own reporting and press are the only per-bank source since the rebrand.

source_name: Райффайзен Банк Аваль — застарілий домен звітності ex.aval.ua
why_relevant: Legacy Aval reporting archive holding pre-rebrand annual reports with historical card/ATM/POS series; valuable for time series back to the 2000s-2010s.

source_name: SMIDA / stockmarket.gov.ua — база розкриття інформації емітентів (НКЦПФР)
why_relevant: Machine-readable XML annual/quarterly issuer reporting for every Ukrainian bank constituted as a joint-stock company — a single systematic entry point to per-bank disclosures, including smaller banks with no real IR site.

source_name: Мінфін (minfin.com.ua) — банківський розділ і картки компаній
why_relevant: Aggregator that reliably re-publishes and links bank annual reports, press releases and reporting pages; the fastest way to discover that a given bank has released a report and to reach the primary URL.

source_name: FINBALANCE — галузеве видання про банки
why_relevant: Specialist Ukrainian banking outlet that reports individual bank results and disclosures in detail, often quoting figures from documents before they are indexed elsewhere.

source_name: Euromoney Awards for Excellence — Ukraine country write-ups
why_relevant: Award submissions force banks to hand over acquiring turnover, terminal counts and growth rates; the published write-ups therefore surface bank-supplied payments metrics (e.g. PrivatBank acquiring UAH 1.06trn in 2024, UAH 973bn via stationary merchant terminals) that appear in no Ukrainian-language document.

source_name: Ukrainian Processing Centre (UPC) — Clients page
why_relevant: UPC is Ukraine's largest third-party card processor (Raiffeisen Bank International group). Its clients page is a reference-customer list naming banks and PSPs it processes for, which maps issuing/acquiring relationships that are otherwise unpublished, and snowballs into further bank actors.

source_name: NBU Payment Infrastructure Register — payment systems, participants and technological operators of payment services
why_relevant: The NBU register is the authoritative roster of technological operators of payment services (the legal category most processors/vendors must register under to serve Ukrainian banks). It converts the vendor landscape from guesswork into an enumerable list, and each register entry links to the operator's own site and its bank partners.

source_name: Printec Ukraine (ТОВ «Прінтек Україна Ел.Ел.Сі.») — corporate site
why_relevant: Printec is a major CEE supplier of ATMs, self-service and POS terminals into Ukrainian banks (reported supplier of ATMs to Ukrgasbank; first certified Checkbox partner for the Castles S1F2 Android terminal). Its site and news carry deployment announcements, product certifications and partner claims — direct evidence of installed-base movement.

source_name: Printec Ukraine LLC — filed management report (financial statements PDF)
why_relevant: A vendor's own statutory management report is a rare quantitative window on the Ukrainian ATM/POS supply market: revenue by line, customer concentration, market commentary. Establishes that the group publishes local-entity filings, which is a repeatable annual series.

source_name: RENOME SMART — ATM/self-service vendor case studies and cash-centre solutions
why_relevant: Rivne-based Ukrainian manufacturer/integrator of ATMs, recyclers, deposit safes and cash-centre software. Publishes named deployment case studies (ProCredit Bank smart branches; ~200 NFC ATMs at Alfa-Bank Ukraine) and states a 31-city service footprint — deployment sizes and bank names that appear nowhere else.

source_name: AVTOKASSA (АВТОКАСА) — cash-handling automation software for banks
why_relevant: Niche Ukrainian vendor of cash-processing/CIT software (collection request workflow for branches, banknote authenticity checking with serial-number reports). Directly relevant to cash-usage and cash-logistics intelligence, and its module list reveals how Ukrainian banks actually run cash operations.

source_name: CS Ltd — CBS B2 core banking system (Ukraine)
why_relevant: Dominant Ukrainian core-banking vendor; publicly claims CBS B2 is used by 62% of Ukrainian banks including 10 of 15 systemically important ones. Vendor-published penetration figures are a rare quantitative proxy for bank IT market share and a pointer to the client banks themselves.

source_name: SNVF ARGUS (СНВФ «АРГУС») — ABS BIS GRANT core banking
why_relevant: Second Ukrainian core-banking vendor, claims first NBU conformity certification for its ABS. Useful as the counterweight to CS Ltd for estimating core-banking market split, and its site documents NBU software conformity requirements that shape all bank IT procurement.

source_name: TAS Link (ТОВ «ТАС ЛІНК») — third-party processor, news and regulatory disclosures
why_relevant: Visa/Mastercard-certified TPP/MSP serving Ukrainian banks with card issuing, acquiring, ATM and POS infrastructure; named by the NBU as one of three systemically important technological operators. Publishes operator disclosures (PDF) and news announcing bank wins and infrastructure scope.

source_name: ProCard (Процесинговий центр «Прокард»)
why_relevant: Independent Ukrainian processing centre offering authorisation/clearing to partner banks. Third data point on the domestic processing market alongside UPC and TAS Link; partner and service pages indicate which smaller banks outsource processing.

source_name: PSM7 (payspacemagazine UA) — review of Ukraine's processing centres
why_relevant: Ukrainian fintech trade outlet that periodically inventories processing centres and payment-tech vendors with comparative figures. Excellent snowball hub: single articles enumerate the vendor field and link to each actor's site.

source_name: Checkbox — certified payment-terminal partner blog (Printec / Castles S1F2)
source_subtype: software partner announcements / certified hardware list
why_relevant: Ukraine's PRRO (fiscalisation) layer means POS terminal models must be certified with software providers like Checkbox. Certification announcements reveal which terminal makes/models are actually entering the Ukrainian market and which distributors are pushing them — an indirect but timely POS installed-base signal.

source_name: Tietoevry Banking — Ukraine open-banking campaign and UPC partnership
why_relevant: International core/card vendor with an explicit Ukraine go-to-market page and a named partnership with UPC to run Ukraine's open-banking platform. Vendor campaign pages of this kind carry regulatory-deadline framing and client counts that indicate where bank IT spend is heading.

source_name: OpenWay Group — Way4 customer case studies
why_relevant: Way4 is the card-processing platform behind Oschadbank's in-house processing centre (per AUB reporting). OpenWay publishes detailed named case studies with deployment scale, making it a route into Ukrainian bank processing architecture and migration events.

source_name: BPC Banking Technologies — SmartVista solutions (Ukraine office)
why_relevant: BPC maintains a Ukraine office and SmartVista is a long-standing switch/card-management platform in the region. Vendor pages and press announcements identify which Ukrainian banks run SmartVista for issuing, acquiring, ATM driving and switching.

source_name: Diebold Nixdorf — DN Series success stories / customer case studies
why_relevant: One of the two global ATM OEMs whose hardware sits under Ukrainian bank fleets (often delivered via local partners such as Renome-Smart, historically Wincor Nixdorf channel). Case studies give fleet sizes, recycling adoption and branch-transformation metrics for CEE that bound Ukrainian estimates.

source_name: Yavir-2000 (Явір-2000) — ATM security and component supplier
why_relevant: Ukrainian supplier of ATM protection systems and ATM components to banks. Wartime ATM physical-security spend is a distinctive Ukrainian market segment; this vendor's pages evidence demand and name the bank-security requirements driving fleet refresh.

source_name: PC Week/UE — Banking IT Summit (Банківський ІТ САМІТ)
source_subtype: industry event / sponsor and speaker listings
why_relevant: The main Ukrainian bank-IT conference: its sponsor lists, speaker rosters and agendas are a compact annual census of which vendors and integrators are actively selling into Ukrainian banks, plus the topics banks are buying. Classic pointer source that snowballs into vendors invisible to search.
